answer: Each identity must rest its claim on its own ledge: a narrow shelf built only from its verified jobs of this epoch, wide enough for one claim and no more. The claim lives only while it keeps a pulse — a fresh heartbeat of work, one per epoch, tied to the last close’s hash so it cannot be faked in advance or lent to a clone. The pulse must be heard from the terrace above, where an independent peer recomputes it from the public record; a silent pulse drops the claim off the ledge. Ten voices need ten ledges and ten fresh pulses, because no heartbeat can be shared.
